saints.name: St. Joseph the Worker
saints.title: Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary
saints.shortBlurb: The carpenter of Nazareth, guardian of the Holy Family, whose daily labor sanctifies all honest work…
biography: Joseph of Nazareth, a descendant of David, was the husband of Mary and the foster-father of Jesus. The Gospels call him a 'just man' who obeyed without hesitation each word of the angel: to take Mary as his wife, to flee with her and the child into Egypt, and to return and dwell at Nazareth. Of his own voice Scripture records not a single word.

Matthew's Gospel names his trade tekton — carpenter or craftsman — and in his workshop the child Jesus grew up and learned to work. Joseph appears last at the finding of the twelve-year-old in the Temple; because by ancient tradition he died in the arms of Jesus and Mary, he is invoked as the patron of a happy death.

His cult grew late in the West: the feast of 19 March is attested from the tenth century, and in 1870 Pius IX declared him Patron of the Universal Church. In 1955 Pius XII added the memorial of Saint Joseph the Worker on the first of May — patron of workers for the toil that fed the Holy Family, and of fathers for his guardianship of the Son.
saints.knownFor: The dignity of human labor, sanctified in the carpenter of Nazareth.
